info.title: Peerdom Public API
info.description:
### Purpose
Peerdom’s RESTful API offers organizations another way to work with the data they manage in Peerdom, making it easy to integrate with other tools or automate processes.

### API Access Requirements
API access is available only to organizations with an active paid subscription or during an active trial period. Organizations upgrade to Peerdom+ to gain access.

Create your API key in your organization’s settings.

Peerdom's API URL is https://api.peerdom.app/

### Authentication
All API endpoints operate in the context of a single organization, determined by the API key you provide. Most endpoints require this key to return data.

Include your API key in the request header using:
```X-Api-Key```.   

### Data Encoding
The API returns JSON-encoded data. Apply any additional encoding needed for your specific context (for example, escape HTML tags when rendering in a browser).

tags.description: API endpoints related to Pages. A page is a titled, ordered collection of cards. Cards are a separate resource (see the Cards tag) linked to pages via the page-card endpoints, so one card can appear on several pages ("mirrored"). Deleting a page archives it rather than removing it, matching the Peerdom app.

post.description:
Create a new peer within the organization's namespace.

When `email` is set, an account is provisioned for the peer and granted a
permission in your organization (see `permissionGroup`). No invitation
email is sent — invite the peer from the Peerdom UI when you are ready.

A Peerdom account is identified globally by its email address, so if one
already exists for that address it is reused and linked, rather than a
second account being created. The existing account is not modified: its
password, and any access it holds in other organizations, are untouched.
Only a permission in *your* organization is added.

requestBody.description:
Create one peer (single object) or many peers (array, 1..n). An array
is created atomically: all peers are created or none are.

201.description:
Created peer. A single object returns the created peer; an array
request returns a creation summary.

409.description:
The peer could not be created because the email address is already in
use. Either a peer in this organization already has it, or the account
for it already holds a different permission here, or it is already
linked to another peer. On an array request the whole batch is rolled
back and the failing item's index is reported.

post.description:
Set (upload or replace) a peer's profile photo. The image is resized
and stored, and the peer's `avatarUrl` is updated. Provide the image in
one of two ways on this single endpoint:

  - `multipart/form-data` with a `file` field (raw image bytes), or
  - `application/json` with an `imageUrl` the server fetches itself.

For `imageUrl` the fetch is restricted for safety: HTTPS only, public
hosts only (private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses
are rejected), a few redirects at most, and a short timeout.

Allowed formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP. Maximum size 5 MB and maximum
dimensions 4000x4000 pixels. Uploading the same image again is a no-op.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the peer whose photo to set

file.description: Image file (JPEG, PNG or WebP). Max 5 MB, max 4000x4000 px.

imageUrl.description:
Public HTTPS URL of the image (JPEG, PNG or WebP). The host
must resolve to a public address. Max 5 MB, max 4000x4000 px.

200.description: peer response with the updated avatarUrl

delete.description:
Remove a peer's profile photo. The peer's `avatarUrl` is cleared and the
stored image is retired. Returns the updated peer. Calling this on a peer
with no photo is a no-op and still returns `200`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the peer whose photo to remove

200.description: peer response with the photo removed (no `avatarUrl`)

post.summary: Assign holders to several roles in one request
post.description:
Assign peers to multiple roles in a single atomic request. The body is an
array of `{roleId, holders[]}` groups; every assignment across every group
is created in one transaction (all-or-none). Collapses what used to be one
call per role into a single round trip.

created.description: Total number of holders created across all roles.

post.summary: Mirror a role into one or more parent circles
post.description:
Create mirrored copies of a role across the given target parent circles.
Every copy shares the source role's template, so the whole mirror group
keeps its custom fields and goals in sync — editing one propagates to all
siblings. If the source role is still standalone, a template is created
and the source is linked to it on the first mirror.

Holders are NOT mirrored. When `copyHolders` is true the source's current
holders are copied onto each new role once, at creation; later holder
changes do not propagate between mirrored roles.

A target circle that already holds a member of the group — including the
source role's own parent circle — is rejected with `400`, so the role is
never duplicated within a circle it is already present in.

The operation is atomic: either every copy is created or none are.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: ID of the source role to mirror.

201.description:
Creation summary. `templateId` is the mirror-group handle shared by
the source and all copies; `items` are the created roles.

templateId.description: The shared template id identifying the mirror group.

404.description: Source role or a target parent circle was not found.

200.description: The roles that make up the mirror group.

post.description:
Create a project for the organization. Optionally attach it to a circle
(`circleId`) and/or nest it under a parent project (`parentId`). Requires
the Projects app to be enabled.

get.description: Get a single project based on the supplied ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of project to fetch

patch.description:
Patch a project. Every field is optional; only the supplied fields are
changed. Renaming regenerates the slug. Requires the Projects app.

post.description:
Create a goal attached to a circle (`nodeId`). The goal `data` carries its
name, order and completion (isComplete or subgoals). Requires the Goals
app to be enabled.

patch.description:
Patch a goal. Every field is optional; only the supplied fields change.
`nodeId` re-attaches the goal to a different circle. Requires the Goals app.

delete.description: Delete a goal and its circle links. Requires the Goals app.

Activate an app for the organization. Idempotent: activating an
already-enabled app succeeds without side effects. Only flips the

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the app to activate.

200.description: The app and its (now enabled) state.

404.description: The organization could not be found.

get.description:
List the organization's custom-field definitions (the schema/vocabulary,
not the per-entity values). Call this before writing peers/roles/groups so
source data maps to the organization's real field names. Optionally filter
by the owning entity with `?entity=`.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: Only return definitions for this owning entity.

post.description:
Create one definition (single object) or many (array, 1..n). An array is
created atomically: all definitions are created or none are. Create the
definitions before setting their values on peers/roles/groups.

201.description:
Created definition. A single object returns the created definition; an
array request returns a creation summary.

get.description:
Fetch a single definition by id, including its `type`, `multiEntry`,
`entity` and `nodeType`, so values can be verified before being written.

patch.description:
Update side-effect-free fields of a definition: `name` (the API key used
to write values by name), `translation` (display labels), `order` and
`public`. A rename updates BOTH the API key and the label. `type`,
`entity`, `nodeType`, `multiEntry` and `relationScope` are not editable
here — changing them would mutate or drop existing values — and are
rejected with 400.

delete.description: Delete a definition and, via cascade, every value stored against it.

post.summary: Import peers, groups, roles and holders in one request
post.description:
Apply a single JSON document that creates peers, groups, roles and holder
assignments together, atomically (all-or-none). Entities created in the
same document are wired together with transient `ref` aliases: give an item
a `ref`, then point at it from a parent (`parentRef`) or a holder
(`roleRef` / `peerRef`). Aliases are in-memory only and never stored. Items
that already exist can be referenced by real id instead. Synchronous — keep
batches reasonably sized.

201.description: Import summary (counts of what was processed).

get.description: List the organization's pages, newest-updated first.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Filter by archived state.

parameters.name: public
parameters.description: Filter by public/private.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: Comma-separated expansions. `cards` embeds the page's ordered cards.

patch.description: Update a page's name, description, visibility or archived state.

delete.description: Archives the page (sets `archived: true`). The page is NOT hard-deleted — it remains fetchable and can be restored with `PATCH { "archived": false }`.

get.description: List the cards on a page, in their per-page order.

post.summary: Attach a card to a page
post.description: Link an existing card to a page. `mirrored` links the same card, so edits propagate to every page that shares it; `independent` (default) clones the card first, so edits do not propagate.

200.description: The card was already linked to this page (idempotent no-op for a mirrored card); the existing link is returned unchanged.

put.description: Rewrite the order of a page's cards. Send the FULL, ordered list of the page's current card ids; each card's position becomes its array index.

200.description: The page's cards in their new order.

delete.summary: Unlink a card from a page
delete.description: Removes the card from this page only. The card itself, and its links to any other pages, are unaffected. To delete the card entirely use DELETE /cards/{id}.

204.description: The card was unlinked from the page.

parameters.name: onPage
parameters.description: Only cards linked to this page.

post.description: Create a text or image card. Image cards accept the image EITHER as a `multipart/form-data` `file` field OR as an `imageUrl` in a JSON body (fetched server-side). Link the card to a page afterwards via POST /pages/{id}/cards.

get.description: Fetch a card, including `pageCount` (how many pages share it).

patch.description: Edit a card's content. The change applies to EVERY page the card is linked to (mirrored cards share one content row). `type` may be switched between `text` and `image`.

delete.description: Permanently delete the card, its content, and every page link (it disappears from all pages). To remove a card from a single page without deleting it, use DELETE /pages/{id}/cards/{cardId}.

slug.description: Auto-generated from the name; unique per organization.

public.description: True iff visibility is PUBLIC. The only visibility axis writable via this API.

visibility.description: Underlying page visibility. Read-only here — only the PUBLIC axis is settable via `public`. SHARED (per-account grants) cannot be set through this API, so setting `public: false` on a SHARED page is a no-op (it stays SHARED).

createdBy.description: Email of the account that created the page.

cards.description: Present only when requested via `?with=cards`; ordered by page position.

order.description: The card's position on a page. Present only when the card is read in a page context.

pageCount.description: How many pages share this card (>1 means mirrored). Present on GET /cards/{id}.

CardContent.description: Shape depends on the card type — text {text,isQuote} or image {imageUrl,imageAlt}.

imageUrl.description: For image cards: a public https URL, fetched server-side.

type.description: Switch the card between text and image.

CardCreateMultipart.description: Multipart form for uploading an image card's bytes directly.

mode.description: `mirrored` links the same card (edits propagate); `independent` clones it.

order.description: Optional insert position; appended to the end when omitted.

cardIds.description: The full, ordered list of the page's current card ids.

liveMapId.description: The tenant's live (non-draft) map id, or null if it has none yet.

palette.description: The tenant's curated color palette. When `allowPersonalColors` is false, node/group colors must be one of these hex values; use them to know which colors are available before creating or updating nodes.

hex.description: The color as a lowercase `#RRGGBB` hex string.

allowPersonalColors.description: When false, node/group colors are restricted to `palette`. When true, any valid hex color may be used.

private.description: Set to true to make the draft map private; set to false to keep it public.

circleId.description: Optional circle (node) to attach the project to.

parentId.description: Optional parent project to nest under.

ProjectUpdate.description: All fields optional; only supplied fields are changed.

isComplete.description: Whole-goal completion, used when no subgoals are present.

nodeId.description: The circle (node) the goal attaches to.

GoalUpdate.description: All fields optional; only supplied fields are changed.

nodeId.description: Re-attach the goal to this circle.

email.description: The peer's email address, when one is on record. Omitted for peers without an address.

joinedAt.description: When the peer joined (the record's creation date).

leftAt.description: When the peer left. Omitted for active peers; present for former peers (see the `includeFormer` query parameter).

roles.description: The roles this peer holds. Only included when requested via `?with=roles` on `GET /peers/{id}`.

contribution.description: Contribution App needs to be enabled for this attribute.

contributionUnit.description: Contribution App needs to be enabled for this attribute.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a peer. If there are none, the attribute is not shown.

id.description: The unique identifier for the custom field.

name.description: The name of the custom field definition.

values.description: The custom field value(s). Always an array, even for single-entry fields. For relation-type fields these are the raw ids of the linked entities; see `relations` for the resolved names.

relations.description: Only present on relation-type custom fields. Each stored id resolved against the linked entity (peer, role/circle, or page), tenant-scoped. `name` is null when the id no longer resolves (deleted or cross-tenant), which lets a verify-after-write client distinguish a real link from a dangling one.

email.description: The peer's email address. When provided on create, an account is found-or-created and linked to the peer, and a tenant permission is granted (see `permissionGroup`). No invitation email is sent — the account lands in a pending-invite state and is invited later from the Peerdom UI. When omitted, an account-less ("chart-only") peer is created.

percentage.description: Contribution App needs to be enabled for this attribute.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a peer. You can add the properties from the predefined custom fields. Please refer to the example in the sample request.

permissionGroup.description:
Permission granted to the account provisioned for this peer. Requires `email` — an account-less peer has no account to grant a permission to, so sending this without one is rejected with a 400 rather than silently ignored.

Defaults to `guest`, matching a CSV import with an empty access rights column. Subject to the tenant's seat/license limit — on a PBS-subscribed tenant with no seats remaining it is downgraded to `guest`, so the permission actually granted may be lower than the one requested.

Create-only. Sending it on `PUT /peers/{id}` is rejected with a 400; changing an existing peer's permission is done from the Peerdom UI.

data.description: The name of the custom field definition.

percentComplete.description: required when the type is percentage

isComplete.description: required when the type is boolean

amountComplete.description: required when the type is numeric

targetAmount.description: required when the type is numeric

color.description: The choice of color for the node as a hex string (`#RRGGBB` or `#RGB`). When the tenant's color palette is enforced (the `allowPersonalColors` setting is off), the color must match one of the palette's colors, otherwise the request is rejected with 400. When personal colors are allowed, any valid hex is accepted.

representing.description: The node this role represents (its represented parent). Only included when requested via `?with=representing`.

templateId.description:
The mirror-group handle: the id of the shared `NodeTemplate`. Roles
with the same `templateId` form one mirror group and keep their
custom fields and goals in sync. Absent for standalone (non-mirrored)
roles.

target.description: The role's contribution target (`Node.targetPercentage`), expressed in the tenant's contribution unit (same conversion as holder `contribution`). Only present when the Contribution App is enabled; null when no target is set.

contributionUnit.description: The contribution unit the `target` is expressed in. Only present when the Contribution App is enabled.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a role. If there are none, the attribute is not shown.

id.description: The unique identifier for the custom field.

name.description: The name of the custom field definition.

values.description: The custom field value(s). Always an array, even for single-entry fields.

contribution.description: Contribution App needs to be enabled for this attribute. Value 0 means that either a contribution of 0 is stored, or none is stored.

contributionUnit.description: Contribution App needs to be enabled for this attribute.

purpose.description: The role's purpose. Sourced from the default "Purpose" custom field; omitted if unset or if the tenant renamed that field.

accountabilities.description: The role's accountabilities. Sourced from the default "Responsibilities" custom field; omitted if unset or if the tenant renamed that field.

groups.description: The role's parent group (circle). Only included when requested via `?with=groups`. A role has a single direct parent, so this contains at most one entry.

color.description: The choice of color for the node as a hex string (`#RRGGBB` or `#RGB`). When the tenant's color palette is enforced (the `allowPersonalColors` setting is off), the color must match one of the palette's colors, otherwise the request is rejected with 400. When personal colors are allowed, any valid hex is accepted.

shape.description: Specifies the shape of the node. Acceptable values are "circle" or "hexagon", each determining the visual representation of the node within the interface.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a group. If there are none, the attribute is not shown.

id.description: The unique identifier for the custom field.

name.description: The name of the custom field definition.

values.description: The custom field value(s). Always an array, even for single-entry fields.

parentId.description: The Id should be a valid group ID. In order to find the groups on your map, please check these routes [Get a list of groups](#operation/getGroups). For roles, kindly visit this route [Get a list of roles](#operation/getRoles)

external.description: Marks the node as outside the organization. It also controls the parent link (there is no direct `parentId: null`): setting `external` to true DETACHES the node from its parent (it becomes top-level); setting it to false re-attaches it under the map's root circle. Conversely, supplying a `parentId` on a currently-external node flips `external` back to false.

color.description: The choice of color for the node as a hex string (`#RRGGBB` or `#RGB`). When the tenant's color palette is enforced (the `allowPersonalColors` setting is off), the color must match one of the palette's colors, otherwise the request is rejected with 400. When personal colors are allowed, any valid hex is accepted.

shape.description: Specifies the shape of the node. Acceptable values are "circle" or "hexagon", each determining the visual representation of the node within the interface.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a group/role. You can add the properties from the predefined custom fields. Please refer to the example in the sample request.

representingId.description: Id of the group the new role represents (must be the role's parent group).

target.description: The role's contribution target, mapped to `Node.targetPercentage`. A percentage where 100 = 1.0 FTE (consistent with holder `percentage`), so it can express multi-FTE targets. `null` clears it. Requires the Contribution App to be enabled.

targetParentIds.description: Ids of the parent circles to mirror the role into. Each must be an existing circle in your tenant.

copyHolders.description:
When true, the source role's current holders are copied onto each
mirrored role at creation. This is a one-time snapshot, NOT a mirror:
unlike custom fields and goals, holder changes do not propagate
between mirrored roles afterwards.

color.description: The choice of color for the node as a hex string (`#RRGGBB` or `#RGB`). When the tenant's color palette is enforced (the `allowPersonalColors` setting is off), the color must match one of the palette's colors, otherwise the request is rejected with 400. When personal colors are allowed, any valid hex is accepted.

parentId.description: The Id should be a valid group/role ID. In order to find the groups on your map, please check these routes [Get a list of groups](#operation/getGroups). For roles, kindly visit this route [Get a list of roles](#operation/getRoles)

external.description: Marks the node as outside the organization. It also controls the parent link (there is no direct `parentId: null`): setting `external` to true DETACHES the node from its parent (it becomes top-level); setting it to false re-attaches it under the map's root circle. Conversely, supplying a `parentId` on a currently-external node flips `external` back to false.

shape.description: Specifies the shape of the node. Acceptable values are "circle" or "hexagon", each determining the visual representation of the node within the interface.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a group/role. You can add the properties from the predefined custom fields. Please refer to the example in the sample request.

color.description: The choice of color for the node as a hex string (`#RRGGBB` or `#RGB`). When the tenant's color palette is enforced (the `allowPersonalColors` setting is off), the color must match one of the palette's colors, otherwise the request is rejected with 400. When personal colors are allowed, any valid hex is accepted.

parentId.description: The Id should be a valid group/role ID. In order to find the groups on your map, please check these routes [Get a list of groups](#operation/getGroups). For roles, kindly visit this route [Get a list of roles](#operation/getRoles)

external.description: Marks the node as outside the organization. It also controls the parent link (there is no direct `parentId: null`): setting `external` to true DETACHES the node from its parent (it becomes top-level); setting it to false re-attaches it under the map's root circle. Conversely, supplying a `parentId` on a currently-external node flips `external` back to false.

customFields.description: The custom fields for a group/role. You can add the properties from the predefined custom fields. Please refer to the example in the sample request.

shape.description: Specifies the shape of the node. Acceptable values are "circle" or "hexagon", each determining the visual representation of the node within the interface.

representing.description: The Id of the group the role represents, or null to clear it.

representingAll.description: If true, the change to the above field "representing" will be copied to all the mirrored nodes.

electable.description: Set the value to true, if the role is electable.

target.description: The role's contribution target, mapped to `Node.targetPercentage`. A percentage where 100 = 1.0 FTE (consistent with holder `percentage`). `null` clears it. Requires the Contribution App to be enabled.

BulkHolderAssignment.description: One group in a bulk holder assignment — a role and the holders to assign to it.

ImportMap.description:
A single import document. Entities created here can reference each other via
transient `ref` aliases (parentRef / roleRef / peerRef) or via real ids.

mapId.description: Target map for the groups/roles in this import.

ref.description: Transient alias for referencing this peer from holders in the same document.

parentRef.description: Alias of a group created earlier in this document (alternative to parentId).
Alias of a group created earlier in this document (alternative to parentId).

roleRef.description: Alias of a role created earlier in this document (alternative to roleId).

peerRef.description: Alias of a peer created earlier in this document (alternative to peerId).

BulkCreateError.description:
Error returned for an atomic bulk (array) create. Because a bulk create
is all-or-none, any failing item rolls back the whole batch and nothing
is persisted. `errors` identifies the offending item(s) by their index
in the request array.

index.description: Zero-based index of the failing item in the request array.

Translation.description: Localized labels keyed by language code.

entity.description: The kind of entity this field is attached to.

nodeType.description: When `entity` is `node`, narrows to circle/role (or generic).

multiEntry.description: Whether the field accepts multiple values.

relationScope.description: Present only for `relation` fields — what the relation points to.

CustomFieldDefinitionUpdate.description:
Editable fields for a rename / edit. All optional; only the supplied
fields are changed. Any other field (e.g. `type`, `multiEntry`) is
rejected with 400.

name.description: The API key used to write values by name.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with an existing resource (e.g. duplicate name).

A bulk (array) create failed. The batch is atomic, so nothing was
persisted; `errors` reports the offending item index(es).
